question: What is the typical duration of the postpartum period known as the puerperium?

options.A: Three months
options.B: Two weeks
options.C: Six weeks
options.D: One year

explanation: The puerperium generally lasts for about six weeks after childbirth, which is the time required for maternal organs to return close to their pre-pregnant state. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h1)

question: Why should a nurse always look at imaging results alongside their own physical assessment of the patient?

options.A: To correlate what is seen on the scan with the patient's actual clinical symptoms
options.B: To legally rewrite the official radiology report if a mistake was made
options.C: To decide whether the patient needs surgery without consulting a doctor
options.D: To replace the radiologist's formal interpretation with nursing judgment

explanation: Pictures don't tell the whole story! Combining scan results with what the patient is actually feeling (like pain or swelling) helps you provide top-notch care. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T5#GNS222_U1_T5_h8)

question: Why is putting in a large-bore intravenous (IV) line such an urgent priority when managing severe PPH?

options.A: To provide a pathway for total parenteral nutrition
options.B: To make it easy to give routine pain relief
options.C: To allow rapid running of IV fluids and blood products
options.D: To monitor central venous pressure continuously

explanation: When a mother is losing blood quickly, every second counts. Wide IV lines let you pump in lifesaving fluids and blood fast enough to beat shock. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h6)

question: Why must nurses ask patients about their family planning or contraceptive methods?

options.A: To replace the need for asking about sexual partners
options.B: To judge the personal lifestyle choices of the patient
options.C: To evaluate pregnancy prevention methods and potential hormone side effects
options.D: To determine how much tax the patient pays

explanation: No judgment here—just good nursing! Asking about contraception helps us understand cycle changes, check for side effects, and support the patient's family goals. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T3#GNS311_U1_T3_h5)

question: How do safe youth clubs and recreational activities help prevent substance abuse?

options.A: By providing legal access to prescription medications
options.B: By completely eliminating all life challenges and pressures
options.C: By forcing adolescents to study chemistry all day
options.D: By giving teenagers healthy ways to manage stress and stay engaged

explanation: Spot on! Fun, positive activities keep youth active, boost their self-esteem, and give them great outlets to handle stress instead of turning to drugs. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T13#GNS312_U3_T13_h7)

question: Why do we use skin traction right after a bone fracture?

options.A: To speed up the growth of new skin cells
options.B: To completely eliminate the need for pain medication
options.C: To permanently heal the bone without surgery
options.D: To relieve painful and violent muscle spasms

explanation: Steady pulling tires out the muscles around the break, stopping those painful spasms that pull the bone ends out of place. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T8#GNS221_U1_T8_h2)

question: Why do modern surgical wards prefer closed drainage systems over open ones?

options.A: They completely stop the patient from feeling any surgical pain
options.B: They significantly lower the risk of outside bacteria entering the body
options.C: They allow the surgical wound to heal without any dressings at all
options.D: They never require the nurse to empty or measure the collected fluid

explanation: Think of closed systems as sealed packages—because they are closed to the outside air, germs have a much harder time getting in to cause an infection. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h2)

question: Why must nurses check a patient's liver function before starting a long course of albendazole?

options.A: Healthy liver function prevents worms from entering the bloodstream
options.B: Liver cells store the medication for up to six months
options.C: Hepatic enzymes are needed to activate the drug in the stomach
options.D: The medication is metabolized primarily through the liver

explanation: Brilliant! Because the liver breaks down these drugs, we need to make sure it's healthy enough to handle the workload without causing toxicity. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h7)

question: Which serious complication of a peptic ulcer causes a hard, board-like abdomen and severe pain?

options.A: Pyloric stenosis
options.B: Perforation
options.C: Pernicious anemia
options.D: Gastric reflux

explanation: Spot on! If an ulcer burns right through the stomach wall, stomach contents leak into the belly, causing a medical emergency with a very rigid, painful abdomen. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h3)

question: What color should the nurse tell the patient their stool might appear for a few days after a barium swallow?

options.A: Bright red or bloody
options.B: Jet black and tarry
options.C: Neon green or yellow
options.D: Chalky white or light gray

explanation: The elimination of residual unabsorbed barium sulfate naturally turns the stool a pale, chalky white or gray color until it is completely cleared. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h7)

question: Which part of the loop of Henle allows water to leave freely via osmosis?

options.A: The ascending limb
options.B: The collecting duct
options.C: The distal convoluted tubule
options.D: The descending limb

explanation: The descending limb of the loop of Henle is permeable to water, letting water flow out into the high-osmolarity medullary tissue. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h7)

question: As a nurse, you receive new paracetamol expiring in 2026, but the shelf already has stock expiring in 2025. What should you do?

options.A: Place the 2025 stock in front and dispense it before the 2026 stock
options.B: Mix all the tablets together in one big container
options.C: Return both supplies immediately to the central medical store
options.D: Place the 2026 stock in front and keep the 2025 stock behind

explanation: Great clinical habit! Always use the ones expiring sooner (2025) so nothing spoils on the shelf. That's true nursing resourcefulness. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a goal of a strong healthcare referral network?

options.A: Isolating the client from all family and friends
options.B: Ensuring continuity of medical follow-up
options.C: Providing access to professional social workers
options.D: Connecting the client with community support groups

explanation: Good referral networks are designed to build a strong safety net and reduce isolation, never to cut a client off from the people who love and support them. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h7)

question: Why does your nose feel so stuffy and congested when you catch a cold?

options.A: Inflammatory mediators cause local blood vessels to dilate and leak fluid into tissues
options.B: Infiltrating bacteria block the normal flow of air through the sinus passages
options.C: The nasal cartilage permanently expands in response to cold temperatures
options.D: Inhaled dust particles accumulate rapidly because cilia stop growing

explanation: When your immune system fights a cold virus, blood vessels in your nose widen and swell up, letting fluid leak into the tissues. This narrows your airway and creates that annoying stuffy feeling! [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h2)

question: A nursing mother in a local clinic asks for an affordable, traditional Nigerian food option that provides both fluid and easy energy during early morning hours. What is a suitable recommendation?

options.A: Raw bitter kola chewed without any water
options.B: A carbonated sugary soft drink with dry biscuits
options.C: Warm pap (akamu) prepared with milk and groundnuts
options.D: Heavy dry gin infused with local roots

explanation: Pap is a traditional, easily digestible meal that provides fluid, warmth, and steady energy when enriched with milk and groundnuts. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h6)

question: Why might some patients with cervical irritation feel absolutely no symptoms at all?

options.A: The inflammatory process can remain mild and localized without triggering pain receptors.
options.B: Hormones in the vagina completely block any physical sensation of swelling.
options.C: The body instantly neutralizes all bacterial toxins before they reach the surface.
options.D: Nerve endings in the cervix are purely motor and never transmit sensory signals.

explanation: Exactly! Mild inflammation often stays quiet without setting off pain signals, which is why regular screening tests are so important for women's health. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h4)

question: Why is it dangerous to keep expired medication anywhere near active stock supplies?

options.A: It creates a high risk of accidentally administering degraded drugs to a patient
options.B: It automatically invalidates the expiry dates of neighboring boxes
options.C: It takes up space that should be used for cleaning supplies
options.D: It causes the electric lights in the storage room to flicker

explanation: Closeness to active stock increases the chance that a busy nurse will grab an expired item during an emergency. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h7)

question: What happens to total maternal serum calcium levels during a normal pregnancy?

options.A: They decrease due to hemodilution and lower albumin
options.B: They increase significantly to support fetal bone growth
options.C: They remain completely unchanged throughout all trimesters
options.D: They drop dangerously low because of kidney failure

explanation: Total serum calcium drops because blood volume expands and blood protein levels fall, but ionized calcium stays normal. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h3)

question: What is a key piece of advice for a patient going home with a chronic bleeding disorder?

options.A: Recognize and report early signs of bleeding like unusual bruising or blood in the stool
options.B: Avoid drinking water entirely to prevent fluid overload in the blood vessels
options.C: Stop taking all prescribed medications once you feel a slight energy improvement
options.D: Engage in high-contact sports to build up your physical strength and endurance

explanation: Teaching patients to spot early warning signs means they can get help before a minor bleed turns into a major emergency. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h7)

question: In the chain of infection, what is the main job of a reservoir?

options.A: It is the natural habitat where pathogens live and multiply
options.B: It is the medication used to kill harmful bacteria
options.C: It is the immune response created by the host
options.D: It is the physical method by which a pathogen enters the body

explanation: Think of a reservoir as the home base where germs hang out, grow, and multiply before they find a new host to infect. You've got this! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h1)

question: Based on how much the body needs them, what are the two main groups of nutrients?

options.A: Macronutrients and micronutrients
options.B: Proteins and carbohydrates
options.C: Organic and inorganic nutrients
options.D: Vitamins and minerals

explanation: You got this! We split nutrients into macronutrients (needed in large amounts like carbs and proteins) and micronutrients (needed in small amounts like vitamins). [learn more](GNS227_U1_T006#GNS227_U1_T006_h1)

question: Why do you inject air into a multi-dose medication vial before you pull out the liquid?

options.A: To kill any bacteria inside the glass vial
options.B: To dilute a medication that is too thick
options.C: To prevent a vacuum from forming inside the vial
options.D: To warm up the medication for the patient

explanation: You got it! Pumping in a little air replaces the space of the liquid you're about to take out, making the drawing process smooth and easy. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T7#GNS122_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the big advantage of using rapid molecular tests like GeneXpert for TB?

options.A: They replace the need for taking a thorough patient history.
options.B: They provide fast results and detect drug resistance early.
options.C: They can cure the infection without any medications.
options.D: They are completely painless and require no patient samples.

explanation: GeneXpert is fantastic because it gives results in just a few hours and tells us right away if the drugs won't work against that specific strain. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T5#GNS214_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why can cultural stigma surrounding dementia make things especially tough for families in Nigeria?

options.A: It guarantees that traditional healers will cure the underlying brain damage
options.B: It forces the government to provide free nursing homes in every state
options.C: It eliminates all forms of physical illness in elderly community members
options.D: It can cause families to hide the affected relative and isolate themselves from support

explanation: Stigma creates shame and secrecy, which stops families from reaching out for the healthcare advice and community support they need. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T10#GNS324_U4_T10_h7)

question: What is the main biological goal of puberty during adolescence?

options.A: Completion of prefrontal cortex myelination
options.B: Rapid increase in bone mineral density only
options.C: Attaining sexual maturity and reproductive capacity
options.D: Stabilization of adult personality traits

explanation: You got this! Puberty is simply the body's natural transition to reach sexual maturity and the ability to reproduce. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why is giving injections straight into the heart a last resort in today's hospitals?

options.A: It requires special oral preparation before injection
options.B: It takes too long for the medication to reach the brain
options.C: It can only be performed by a pharmacist in a laboratory
options.D: It carries severe risks of heart damage and safer routes usually work

explanation: Poking the heart muscle can cause serious bleeding and injury. That's why nurses and doctors always try IV or bone (intraosseous) lines first! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T14#GNS125_U3_T14_h1)

question: A clinic ensures that its facility can be reached easily by rural women and has fair pricing. Which core dimension is being prioritized?

options.A: Effectiveness
options.B: Safety
options.C: Acceptability
options.D: Accessibility

explanation: Correct! Accessibility means services are within physical and financial reach for the mothers and families who need them most. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T4#GNS312_U5_T4_h2)

question: Why is soluble fiber often recommended in the dietary management of faecal incontinence?

options.A: It relaxes the internal sphincter muscle
options.B: It completely stops all digestive activity in the stomach
options.C: It absorbs excess water to form a firmer, more formed stool
options.D: It prevents the absorption of all dietary fats

explanation: Soluble fiber adds bulk and consistency to liquid or loose stools, making them much easier for the sphincters to control. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h6)

question: Why do they sometimes give patients gas-producing crystals along with the barium?

options.A: To numb the throat during swallowing
options.B: To prevent the patient from feeling nauseated by the barium
options.C: To speed up the emptying of the stomach contents
options.D: To provide a double-contrast view of the stomach lining

explanation: Brilliant! The gas blows the stomach open like a balloon, pressing the barium against the walls so we get super-clear pictures. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h5)

question: How do condoms stop sexually transmitted infections from spreading between partners?

options.A: Antibiotics coated on the inside of the sheath
options.B: Chemical destruction of bacteria by latex proteins
options.C: A physical barrier blocking contact with infectious fluids
options.D: Immune system stimulation from the lubricant

explanation: Spot on! The material creates a solid wall so infectious fluids never touch or enter mucous membranes. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h3)

question: Why should you encourage patients to tell you immediately if their IV site starts burning?

options.A: It eliminates the need for the nurse to check the pump
options.B: It allows early detection of infiltration or extravasation
options.C: It proves the patient is paying attention to instructions
options.D: It guarantees the medication is working at maximum speed

explanation: Patients are our best partners! If they speak up early about burning or pain, you can stop the infusion before any real damage happens to their skin. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T5#GNS125_U3_T5_h9)

question: When should a community nurse decide to refer a family planning client?

options.A: A client requesting a routine supply of oral contraceptive pills that are currently in stock
options.B: A client experiencing severe side effects from their current method that require a doctor's care
options.C: A client who attends the clinic for her annual general wellness checkup
options.D: A client who arrives on time for a scheduled injection appointment

explanation: If a client has heavy, unusual complications beyond basic clinic care, it is safest to send them up to a doctor who can help sort it out. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h2)

question: What happens when someone mixes sleeping pills (sedatives) with alcohol?

options.A: Immediate neutralization of all toxic chemicals in the blood
options.B: A sudden increase in physical stamina and alertness
options.C: Severe respiratory suppression and potential breathing failure
options.D: Enhanced absorption of vital nutrients in the stomach

explanation: Spot on! Both alcohol and sedatives slow down the brain. Combining them can make breathing slow down to a dangerous, fatal stop. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why did military nursing groups become so important during the Crusades?

options.A: To translate ancient Greek philosophy texts
options.B: To provide organized shelter and treat wounded soldiers
options.C: To manufacture advanced gunpowder and tactical weapons
options.D: To govern newly conquered political territories

explanation: During the Crusades, special nursing groups were needed to set up safe resting places and care for fighters and travelers who got hurt. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why must you be extra careful when trying to use the basilic vein for venepuncture?

options.A: It lies close to the brachial artery and median nerve
options.B: It carries oxygenated blood directly from the lungs
options.C: It is too small to yield an adequate blood sample
options.D: It has thick muscular walls that resist needle entry

explanation: Be cautious with the basilic vein—major nerves and the brachial artery run right beside it, so care is needed to avoid accidental injury. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h2)

question: Why do community health clinics use standardized monthly reporting templates?

options.A: They replace the need for individual patient client cards
options.B: They allow local health posts to aggregate and transmit data upward to health authorities
options.C: They serve as personal journals for nurses to write daily reflections
options.D: They act as legal contracts between patients and the hospital

explanation: Spot on! Standardized templates make sure data flows smoothly and clearly from local grassroots clinics all the way up to national health planners. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T13#GNS225_U2_T13_h6)

question: A nurse notices an unsteady resident pacing near a cluttered hallway. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Administer a strong sedative medication to keep the resident asleep
options.B: Ignore the situation since walking independently is always encouraged
options.C: Clear the hallway clutter and assist the resident safely back to their seat
options.D: Instruct the resident to run down the hallway to improve agility

explanation: You've got it! Clearing out obstacles right away is a quick, life-saving step to prevent falls. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T2#GNS324_U5_T2_h6)

question: What does measuring stimulated acid output involve during a gastric analysis?

options.A: Giving a medication that prompts the stomach to make acid
options.B: Exercising the patient vigorously on a stationary bicycle
options.C: Feeding the patient a high-fat meal before tube placement
options.D: Flushing the stomach with strong alkaline solutions

explanation: Special medications (like pentagastrin) are given to test the maximum acid-making power of the stomach glands. You are learning clinical diagnostics step by step! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T3#GNS213_U3_T3_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal symptom of the postpartum blues?

options.A: Temporary fatigue from broken sleep patterns
options.B: Mild mood swings and unexpected crying spells
options.C: Severe delusions and thoughts of harming the infant
options.D: Feeling slightly overwhelmed by new responsibilities

explanation: Crying spells and feeling overwhelmed are totally normal as hormones shift. However, delusions or thoughts of hurting the baby are never normal blues—they are signs of a severe emergency like postpartum psychosis. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h6)

question: What behavior might you notice in a patient who has reached acceptance?

options.A: Conserving energy and withdrawing into quiet reflection
options.B: Arguing with family over small things
options.C: Demanding aggressive new experimental treatments
options.D: Denying that they have any symptoms at all

explanation: As energy fades, patients in acceptance often quiet down, letting go of worldly fuss to rest in peace. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T3#GNS221_U4_T3_h6)

question: A newly diagnosed patient is terrified and refuses to talk about medication schedules. What is your best first nursing action?

options.A: Report the patient immediately to local public health authorities
options.B: Withhold all educational materials until the patient asks for them
options.C: Force the patient to swallow the first dose of pills right away
options.D: Provide empathetic, non-judgmental support and address emotional distress

explanation: Empathy first! Building trust and helping patients work through their fear and stigma is always the essential first step before teaching them about medications. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T3#GNS216_U6_T3_h6)

question: When reading a skin test, which specific physical change should you measure?

options.A: Erythema
options.B: Temperature
options.C: Ecchymosis
options.D: Induration

explanation: You nailed it! We measure induration (the hard, raised bump) because that shows a true immune response, whereas simple surface redness doesn't mean a positive result. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T8#GNS125_U3_T8_h5)

question: Why should community health nurses plan health programs *with* the people rather than just *for* them?

options.A: It guarantees that government funding will double instantly
options.B: It completely removes the need to write nursing reports
options.C: It ensures programs respect local culture and gain community support
options.D: It allows the nurse to skip doing fieldwork entirely

explanation: Great thinking! When community members are involved from the start, they trust the process more and the program actually fits their daily lives. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h1)

question: You cannot feel a dying patient's radial pulse at the wrist. What should you do next as the nurse?

options.A: Call the doctor immediately to start IV fluids
options.B: Apply a warm water bottle to their hands
options.C: Pump the blood pressure cuff higher on their arm
options.D: Check a central pulse like the carotid or femoral

explanation: When peripheral circulation gets weak, wrist pulses fade first. Checking a central pulse helps you accurately check the remaining heart activity. You're building great clinical instincts! [learn more](GNS221_U4_T4#GNS221_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is the very first thing you should do when starting a reproductive health chat with a patient?

options.A: Document the patient's exact insurance details
options.B: Ensure physical privacy and a quiet environment
options.C: Review previous laboratory blood test results
options.D: Immediately perform a full physical pelvic exam

explanation: You've got this! Patients need a private, safe space to feel comfortable discussing sensitive topics. Always secure a quiet, private spot first before diving into personal health questions. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T3#GNS311_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why is complete chest recoil important between individual chest compressions?

options.A: It keeps the patient's lungs inflated with fresh air
options.B: It gives the rescuer's tired arm muscles a chance to rest
options.C: It prevents the ribs from fracturing during compressions
options.D: It lets the heart chambers fill back up with blood

explanation: If the chest does not recoil fully, the heart cannot refill properly, making the next compression useless. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which infection control step is absolutely mandatory when nursing a suspected Lassa fever patient?

options.A: Placing every patient in a carpeted, air-conditioned room
options.B: Allowing family members to wash the patient's soiled linens
options.C: Using full personal protective equipment and barrier nursing
options.D: Administering prophylactic antibiotics to all hospital visitors

explanation: Barrier nursing with full PPE is non-negotiable to keep infectious body fluids away from staff and other patients. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T8#GNS214_U1_T8_h8)

question: Which group is usually responsible for creating broad health policies and legal frameworks?

options.A: Youth-led organizations
options.B: Government ministries
options.C: Traditional birth attendants
options.D: Private pharmaceutical companies

explanation: That's right! State and federal health ministries carry the official duty of making health policies and legal structures. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T019#GNS226_U5_T019_h3)

question: What is the main job of an Electronic Medical Record (EMR) in the hospital?

options.A: To replace traditional bedside nursing care with automated robots
options.B: To store a digital version of a patient's medical history and chart
options.C: To publish patient health data on public internet search engines
options.D: To track financial profits and billing for insurance companies

explanation: An EMR is simply the digital upgrade to old paper folders. It keeps all of a patient's history neatly in one place so your team can access it easily! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T9#GNS212_U4_T9_h1)

question: Which nursing intervention is the best example of primary cancer prevention?

options.A: Teaching a patient how to care for a surgical wound after tumor removal
options.B: Helping a newly diagnosed patient manage chemotherapy side effects
options.C: Administering the HPV vaccine to a group of adolescent students
options.D: Scheduling a routine screening mammogram for a 50-year-old woman

explanation: Giving the HPV vaccine prevents a viral infection that can lead to cervical cancer, fitting the definition of primary prevention. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T12#GNS321_U1_T12_h2)

question: In the classic ABCD HIV prevention strategy, what does the letter 'C' stand for?

options.A: Care coordination
options.B: CD4 counting
options.C: Condom use
options.D: Clinical cure

explanation: That's right! 'C' stands for consistent condom use, which blocks the exchange of infectious body fluids during sex. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T9#GNS216_U6_T9_h2)

question: What do we mean by 'nutrient quantification' in nursing and nutrition?

options.A: The process of measuring exact amounts of nutrients in food or the body
options.B: The chemical breakdown of proteins in the stomach
options.C: The calculation of total daily fluid intake and output
options.D: The surgical removal of excess fat tissue from the abdomen

explanation: Think of nutrient quantification as measuring out the exact amounts of nutrients someone eats or needs. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T005#GNS227_U4_T005_h1)

question: What does 'replacement cost pricing' mean in a changing economy?

options.A: Waiting for the government to fix market prices before selling any drugs
options.B: Selling all medicines at half price when they are close to their expiration date
options.C: Pricing drugs based on how much it will cost to buy new stock tomorrow
options.D: Charging patients the exact same price the manufacturer set ten years ago

explanation: Replacement pricing ensures that the money you collect today is enough to buy brand-new stock at current market prices. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h6)

question: Among hospital workers, who usually faces the most immediate, daily exposure to sharps and biological waste?

options.A: Nurses and frontline care providers
options.B: Information technology support staff
options.C: Hospital board directors
options.D: Human resource recruitment officers

explanation: Spot on! As a nurse, you are right at the bedside giving injections, sorting out clinical materials, and managing patient care every single day. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h5)

question: Which part of the nail is responsible for growing new nail cells?

options.A: The nail plate
options.B: The nail matrix
options.C: The cuticle
options.D: The nail bed

explanation: Great job! The nail matrix sits right under the skin at the base and does all the hard work of making new cells that push forward to form your hard nails. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T4#GNS112_U5_T4_h1)

question: Why can it be tricky to diagnose a nutrition problem based only on general tiredness?

options.A: Patients always exaggerate how tired they feel
options.B: Fatigue can be caused by many non-nutritional health conditions
options.C: Nutrient deficiencies never cause tiredness or weakness
options.D: Fatigue only occurs when a person is completely dehydrated

explanation: Feeling tired is a sign of many things—like lack of sleep, stress, or an infection—not just poor food intake. We have to look at the whole picture! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T013#GNS227_U7_T013_h4)

question: Which nerve supplies the main feeling and sensation to the external female genitalia?

options.A: The obturator nerve
options.B: The femoral nerve
options.C: The pudendal nerve
options.D: The sciatic nerve

explanation: Great recall! The pudendal nerve is the main pathway supplying feeling to the perineum and external genitalia. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T1#GNS121_U5_T1_h7)

question: An LTC nurse spends a big part of the shift supervising nursing assistants. What is the main reason for this?

options.A: To minimize direct nurse interaction with residents
options.B: To ensure delegated tasks are performed safely and correctly
options.C: To complete administrative paperwork required by the hospital
options.D: To replace the need for formal care planning meetings

explanation: You got it! As the professional nurse, you lead the care team and oversee assistants to make sure daily tasks like hygiene and safety are done properly. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T9#GNS324_U5_T9_h2)

question: When would a nurse researcher build a conceptual framework instead of using a single theoretical framework?

options.A: When combining ideas from multiple sources to fit a unique study
options.B: When the researcher wants to avoid reading published literature
options.C: When the study has no human participants involved
options.D: When the hospital administration bans the use of theories

explanation: Sometimes one theory isn't enough! When your study has a unique mix of ideas, you blend them together into your own custom conceptual framework. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h3)

question: Which of these is a major social root cause of family vulnerability?

options.A: Attending religious gatherings very often
options.B: Living right next to a teaching hospital
options.C: Economic instability and chronic poverty
options.D: Having many healthy children at home

explanation: Exactly! Poverty strips families of the financial cushion they need to buy food, secure good housing, and pay for hospital bills when sickness strikes. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T19#GNS225_U5_T19_h2)

question: Why is it essential to use a pulse oximeter during a sedated endoscopy?

options.A: To calculate the patient's total blood volume loss
options.B: To measure the exact electrical activity of the heart muscle
options.C: To detect early signs of oxygen shortage or respiratory depression
options.D: To determine when the local anesthetic wears off completely

explanation: Sedatives can sometimes make patients breathe too slowly. The oximeter gives us an early warning if their oxygen levels start dropping so we can act fast. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T2#GNS221_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which of these is a classic example of a structural barrier to health behaviour change?

options.A: The specific age distribution of the community
options.B: Personal stubbornness of the local village chief
options.C: Poor road networks and lack of facility equipment
options.D: A patient's lack of interest in taking medications

explanation: Structural barriers are physical or infrastructural roadblocks—like bad roads or broken clinic gear—that make healthy choices harder to practice. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T27#GNS225_U2_T27_h5)

question: How does promising strict privacy change how teenagers use reproductive health services?

options.A: It guarantees that teenagers will never experience health complications
options.B: It completely replaces the need for parental guidance at home
options.C: It encourages teens to seek early advice, testing, and care
options.D: It legally forces parents to abandon their teenage children

explanation: When teens know their visit is confidential, they feel safe enough to get timely checkups, contraception, or treatment when they need it. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h7)

question: Why is early ambulation strongly encouraged after pelvic surgeries like a hysterectomy?

options.A: It prevents venous stasis and reduces the risk of blood clots
options.B: It forces the surgical incision to heal much faster
options.C: It restores immediate hormonal balance in the body
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for postoperative pain relief

explanation: Getting patients moving early promotes lower extremity circulation, significantly lowering the risk of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T7#GNS311_U1_T7_h6)

question: How can nurses help solve scheduling problems caused by traditional family and caregiving duties?

options.A: By offering clinic hours that accommodate domestic responsibilities
options.B: By charging extra fees for patients who arrive late
options.C: By refusing to treat patients who have caregiving duties
options.D: By keeping clinics open only during standard morning work hours

explanation: Flexible clinic timings make it possible for people juggling heavy caregiving duties to still get the medical care they need. Wonderful thinking! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T22#GNS225_U5_T22_h8)

question: What dangerous emergency can happen if a patient abruptly stops taking their anti-seizure medication?

options.A: Permanent hearing loss
options.B: Status epilepticus
options.C: Acute kidney failure
options.D: Severe muscle wasting

explanation: Stopping anti-seizure drugs suddenly can trigger a dangerous loop of continuous seizures called status epilepticus. Patient education on compliance is a major nursing duty! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T12#GNS222_U4_T12_h5)

question: A patient is taking oral iron pills. What advice should you give them to help their body absorb the iron better?

options.A: Take the supplement with vitamin C or orange juice
options.B: Crush the pills and mix them into a yogurt meal
options.C: Swallow the tablets immediately after drinking a glass of milk
options.D: Take the medication right before going to sleep at night

explanation: Vitamin C is iron's best friend! It creates an acidic environment in the stomach that helps the body absorb oral iron much more effectively. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T6#GNS311_U2_T6_h5)

question: What is the main job of antibiotics in our bodies?

options.A: To treat and manage bacterial infections
options.B: To boost overall red blood cell counts
options.C: To replace lost fluids and electrolytes
options.D: To lower elevated body temperature rapidly

explanation: You got this! Antibiotics are specifically made to hunt down and stop bacteria from causing trouble in the body. They don't touch viruses or fever on their own! [learn more](GNS223_U2_T4#GNS223_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which factor most strongly influences whether a teenager attends routine preventive health screenings?

options.A: The personal political views of the attending pharmacist
options.B: The attitude and logistical support of their parents or guardians
options.C: The brand of soap used in the clinic examination rooms
options.D: The architectural design of the local hospital waiting room

explanation: Because minors rely on adults for transport, funding, and permission, family support is vital for accessing preventive care. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T20#GNS312_U3_T20_h6)

question: Which of these belongs to the physical school environment?

options.A: The academic grading scale used by teachers
options.B: Safe drinking water and functional sanitation
options.C: The political affiliation of the local school board
options.D: Standardized testing schedules for final exams

explanation: Correct! The physical environment is all about tangible surroundings like clean toilets, solid buildings, and safe drinking water. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is the main goal of medical treatment during the early and middle stages of this disease?

options.A: Completely curing the underlying genetic defect
options.B: Slowing disease progression and managing blood pressure
options.C: Regenerating completely healthy new kidney tissue
options.D: Stopping all urine production to rest the body

explanation: Since kidney scarring cannot be undone, the primary goal of treatment is to protect the nephrons we have left and keep the patient stable for as long as possible. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T5#GNS213_U4_T5_h6)

question: Which of the following is a major reason why vital statistics are often incomplete in rural Nigeria?

options.A: Every citizen has a personal digital health computer
options.B: Hospitals refuse to admit pregnant women
options.C: Too many people work as professional statisticians
options.D: Many births and deaths happen at home and go unreported

explanation: Home deliveries and unreported home deaths mean many vital events never make it into official government records. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h6)

question: You check a patient's blood pressure during a routine community outreach. Which level of prevention is this?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Quaternary prevention

explanation: Spot-on! Screening tests like blood pressure checks catch hidden problems early. That is the exact definition of secondary prevention. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T5#GNS123_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is a tracheostomy?

options.A: A tube inserted through the nose into the stomach
options.B: A small incision made in the upper chest wall
options.C: A flexible scope passed down the throat
options.D: A surgical opening made into the trachea

explanation: A tracheostomy involves creating a surgical opening directly into the trachea through the neck. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to changing health behaviors in a community?

options.A: Deeply rooted cultural myths and traditional practices
options.B: Language differences and lack of health literacy
options.C: Immediate access to fully stocked, free community pharmacies
options.D: Severe poverty making healthy choices unaffordable

explanation: You got it! Having easy access to free medical supplies actually helps people practice healthy habits rather than blocking them. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why do we carefully control the speed at which the baby's head is born?

options.A: To ensure the placenta detaches immediately
options.B: To prevent the umbilical cord from snapping
options.C: To give the mother time to drink water
options.D: To prevent severe tearing of the perineum

explanation: Spot on! Guiding the head out slowly gives the perineal tissues time to stretch gently, preventing deep tears. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T006#GNS226_U3_T006_h5)

question: Where does the federal VAPP Act automatically apply right after being signed?

options.A: Lagos State only
options.B: All thirty-six states simultaneously
options.C: Rural communities only
options.D: Federal Capital Territory, Abuja

explanation: Correct! The federal VAPP Act applies directly in the FCT. For other states, their local houses of assembly have to 'domesticate' it first. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T14#GNS312_U4_T14_h2)

question: Why is real-time, chronological documentation especially crucial in an emergency department?

options.A: To reduce the total number of nursing staff needed on the night shift
options.B: Because hospital administrators review every single chart every hour
options.C: Because emergency events happen fast, and real-time notes prevent memory gaps
options.D: So that patients can read their charts immediately while in the waiting room

explanation: Writing things down as they occur ensures accuracy in high-stress situations where details are easily forgotten later. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h8)

question: What is the literal meaning of the medical term neoplasm?

options.A: Inflamed tissue
options.B: Normal healing
options.C: New growth
options.D: Cell death

explanation: The term neoplasm comes from Greek roots meaning new formation or growth, which describes the abnormal tissue mass formed by runaway cell division. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T6#GNS321_U1_T6_h1)

question: What drives the passive movement of water across the lining of the intestines?

options.A: Osmotic gradients created by electrolyte transport
options.B: Direct pumping of water molecules by ATP pumps
options.C: Muscular churning of the large intestine
options.D: Enzymatic breakdown of dietary fiber

explanation: You're right! Water doesn't have its own active pumps in the gut; it simply follows the salt (like sodium) via osmosis—where salt goes, water flows! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T012#GNS227_U1_T012_h6)

question: Why is severe fluid in the abdomen (ascites) a big risk during a liver biopsy?

options.A: It destroys all clotting factors in the blood
options.B: It makes the liver float around, making it hard to hit the target with the needle
options.C: It stops numbing medicine from working on the skin
options.D: It makes the patient stop breathing entirely

explanation: That's right! Too much fluid makes the liver shift position, meaning the needle might miss the spot or accidentally poke something else. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h2)

question: As you gently bend your patient's neck forward, they automatically bend their knees and hips. What sign is this?

options.A: Normal nuchal flexibility
options.B: A positive Brudzinski's sign
options.C: A negative Kernig's sign
options.D: Early signs of a stroke

explanation: That automatic knee-and-hip-bend when the neck goes forward is a classic positive Brudzinski's sign. It's a clear giveaway for irritated meninges! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T17#GNS222_U3_T17_h4)

question: What is the medical term for an infection that jumps naturally from vertebrate animals to humans?

options.A: Iatrogenic disease
options.B: Opportunistic mycosis
options.C: Zoonosis
options.D: Nosocomial infection

explanation: Think 'zoo' for animals! Zoonotic diseases are infections we catch from our animal friends. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T82#GNS214_U1_T82_h3)

question: Which home change is top priority when discharging a patient with serious balance and walking challenges?

options.A: Installing grab bars in the bathroom and removing loose rugs
options.B: Repainting all interior walls in bright, contrasting colors
options.C: Upgrading the home entertainment and television system
options.D: Replacing all hard flooring with thick, plush carpeting

explanation: Falls happen most often at home, especially in slick bathrooms and over sliding rugs. Securing these spots keeps our patients safe after they leave the hospital ward. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T22#GNS222_U3_T22_h7)

question: What is the main goal of surgical debridement in osteomyelitis?

options.A: To fuse the adjacent joints together permanently
options.B: To stretch the limb to make it longer
options.C: To replace all marrow with synthetic polymers
options.D: To remove dead and infected bone tissue

explanation: Debridement is basically a clean-up operation where the surgeon scrapes away all the dead, infected bone that antibiotics alone can't reach. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T18#GNS222_U1_T18_h7)

question: Why is ovarian cancer often tricky to catch in its early stages?

options.A: The ovaries are located deep in the pelvis and early tumors rarely cause symptoms
options.B: Symptoms always mimic a common urinary tract infection
options.C: Blood tests routinely miss the specific markers of early ovarian growth
options.D: Ovarian tissue does not develop abnormal cells until late adulthood

explanation: Because the pelvis gives the ovaries plenty of room to stretch, tumors can grow quite a bit before causing any noticeable pain or pressure. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h1)

question: Which hormone surge right in the middle of the cycle directly triggers ovulation?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Luteinizing Hormone
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Prolactin

explanation: That classic mid-cycle 'LH surge' is the green light that causes the mature ovarian follicle to burst and release the egg! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T6#GNS121_U5_T6_h6)

question: Which bacterial STI is famous for causing a classic, usually painless sore called a chancre in its early stage?

options.A: Chlamydia
options.B: Candidiasis
options.C: Gonorrhoea
options.D: Syphilis

explanation: That's primary syphilis! It loves to throw patients off because the initial sore (chancre) doesn't hurt at all, so people often ignore it. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h2)

question: What do the letters in the CAGE questionnaire stand for?

options.A: Control, Addicted, Grief, Escape
options.B: Crave, Anxiety, Guilt, Energy loss
options.C: Count, Assess, Guide, Evaluate
options.D: Cut down, Annoyed, Guilty, Eye-opener

explanation: The CAGE acronym helps clinicians remember four quick screening questions about cutting down, annoyance, guilt, and morning drinking. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h5)

question: As a nurse, why is it helpful to understand national food policies?

options.A: Clinical nutritional counseling fails if patients cannot access or afford recommended foods
options.B: Nurses decide the specific types of seeds farmers must plant
options.C: Nurses are legally required to inspect commercial farms for safety
options.D: Clinical staff must directly distribute farming money to local villages

explanation: When you give dietary advice to a patient, you have to know what food is actually available and affordable in their community! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T18#GNS214_U1_T18_h1)

question: Why do people trying to quit smoking often get sudden cravings when doing routine things, like drinking morning tea?

options.A: Their physical lungs are suddenly damaged by the beverage steam
options.B: The brain has formed strong behavioral links between those routines and smoking
options.C: Their immune system is reacting to dietary changes
options.D: The tea contains hidden traces of chemical nicotine

explanation: Daily habits act as triggers because the brain links those routines directly to smoking. Recognizing this helps us support patients better! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of using the 'teach-back' method when educating patients?

options.A: Testing the nurse's ability to memorize pharmacological side effects
options.B: Allowing the patient to teach nursing students about herbal remedies
options.C: Checking whether the patient truly understands how to take their medication
options.D: Evaluating the financial cost of drugs prescribed at discharge

explanation: Well done! Instead of just asking 'do you understand?', teach-back has patients explain the instructions in their own words so you know they've got it. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T3#GNS215_U2_T3_h6)

question: What do we call an abnormal, new growth of tissue that forms a tumor?

options.A: Atrophy
options.B: Neoplasm
options.C: Metaplasia
options.D: Hypertrophy

explanation: Great start! A neoplasm is simply an abnormal mass of tissue that grows when cells divide more than they should. Think 'neo' (new) + 'plasma' (formation). You've got this! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T2#GNS321_U1_T2_h1)

question: A patient has high blood insulin levels, but their body cells fail to absorb glucose properly due to faulty receptor signaling. What is this scenario called?

options.A: Extracellular deficiency
options.B: Hormone upregulation
options.C: Insulin resistance
options.D: Second messenger failure

explanation: Insulin resistance occurs when target cells stop responding properly to insulin despite adequate or elevated levels in the blood. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T9#GNS211_U1_T9_h6)

question: What is the safest way to handle a deceased patient's jewelry and cash?

options.A: Document them and hand them to family or hospital administration
options.B: Send them along with the body directly to the mortuary
options.C: Give them to the ward cleaner for safekeeping
options.D: Leave them securely locked inside the bedside drawer

explanation: Valuables must be formally documented and given to the family or administrative authorities to prevent loss or theft. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h5)

question: What is the main point of cough etiquette in a busy clinic waiting area?

options.A: To contain respiratory droplets at the source and stop germ spread
options.B: To prevent the buildup of dust particles on furniture
options.C: To cure patients who suffer from chronic lung diseases
options.D: To eliminate the need for healthcare workers to wear face masks

explanation: Exactly! Catching those droplets early stops airborne bugs from floating around and infecting everyone in the waiting room. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h5)

question: Why are domestic food refrigerators discouraged for storing vaccines?

options.A: They lack doors that can be locked with a padlock
options.B: They are too small to hold more than two vials
options.C: They consume too much electricity for a clinic budget
options.D: They experience wide and unsafe temperature fluctuations

explanation: Food refrigerators are not built to hold steady temperatures within the narrow range required for vaccines. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h2)

question: Why should you check a client's footwear during a home fall-risk assessment?

options.A: Walking in slick socks or smooth slippers greatly increases slip hazards
options.B: Slippers are the only approved footwear for older adults
options.C: Tight shoes prevent the nurse from checking pedal pulses
options.D: Footwear determines the exact financial income of the household

explanation: Slippers with smooth soles or walking around in just socks offer zero grip on tile or wood floors, making falls much more likely. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T8#GNS324_U2_T8_h3)

question: What is the single best way to stop germs from spreading when handling specimens?

options.A: Changing the patient room air filters daily
options.B: Wearing two pairs of sterile gloves at all times
options.C: Spraying the examination table with bleach
options.D: Proper hand hygiene before and after the procedure

explanation: Simple handwashing remains your greatest superpower in infection control. Wash your hands religiously! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T4#GNS112_U6_T4_h2)

question: Which fluid solution is preferred for a standard eye wash?

options.A: Hydrogen peroxide
options.B: Normal saline
options.C: Boric acid drops
options.D: Tap water only

explanation: Normal saline is isotonic, meaning it matches the natural fluid balance of the eye so it won't harm delicate cells while cleaning. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h3)

question: Which group of medications is usually given first to stop a long-lasting seizure?

options.A: Diuretics
options.B: Opioid analgesics
options.C: Beta-blockers
options.D: Benzodiazepines

explanation: Correct! Fast-acting benzodiazepines are the go-to emergency drugs to calm down runaway brain activity quickly. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T10#GNS222_U4_T10_h8)

question: During which weeks of pregnancy is the embryo most sensitive to harmful substances (teratogens) that cause birth defects?

options.A: During gametogenesis before fertilization
options.B: The first week prior to implantation
options.C: The final trimester before birth
options.D: Weeks three through eight during organogenesis

explanation: Correct! Weeks 3 to 8 are when all the major organs are actively forming, making this a critical window where they are most vulnerable. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T3#GNS121_U6_T3_h7)

question: A teenager comes in with severe monthly belly pain but no menstrual bleeding. Which condition is the most likely cause?

options.A: Bacterial vaginosis
options.B: Vaginal agenesis
options.C: Atrophic vaginitis
options.D: Transverse vaginal septum

explanation: Well done! A transverse septum acts like a wall blocking menstrual blood from getting out, leading to trapped blood, swollen tissues, and intense monthly pain even though her uterus is working fine. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T11#GNS216_U5_T11_h2)

question: Which post-WWII law provided funding for hospital construction and indirectly led to the growth of nursing homes?

options.A: The Social Security Amendment
options.B: The Medicare and Medicaid Act
options.C: The Nursing Home Reform Act
options.D: The Hill-Burton Act

explanation: The Hill-Burton Act funded a massive wave of hospital building. Once those hospitals started discharging patients who still needed long-term care, the need for separate nursing homes became super obvious! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T5#GNS324_U5_T5_h2)

question: Which maneuver should you use to open the airway of a patient with a suspected neck injury?

options.A: Jaw-thrust maneuver
options.B: Neck-hyperextension method
options.C: Lateral recovery position
options.D: Head-tilt, chin-lift maneuver

explanation: When a neck injury is suspected, use the jaw-thrust maneuver. It opens the airway gently without bending the vulnerable cervical spine. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T6#GNS321_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why is it often harder for instructors to grade a student's affective domain compared to their cognitive knowledge?

options.A: Clinical instructors are not legally allowed to grade student behavior.
options.B: Students never display their true attitudes while in the clinical setting.
options.C: There are no written rules or guidelines for professional nursing behavior.
options.D: Internal feelings and attitudes must be inferred from observable actions rather than direct measurements.

explanation: Since teachers can't read your mind, they watch how you treat patients and colleagues every day to gauge your professional attitude. You're developing great habits! [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h5)

question: What is the main job of endocrine glands in our body?

options.A: Filtering waste products out of liquid blood
options.B: Secreting hormones directly into the bloodstream
options.C: Producing digestive enzymes for the stomach
options.D: Pumping oxygenated blood to body tissues

explanation: Spot on! Endocrine glands don't use ducts. They release their chemical messengers (hormones) straight into nearby blood vessels to reach organs all over the body. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T15#GNS222_U2_T15_h1)

question: What common facial feature is often seen during the active dying phase because muscles completely relax?

options.A: Flushed cheeks
options.B: A sagging jaw
options.C: Widened eyes
options.D: A tight grimace

explanation: When facial muscles lose all their tone, the jaw naturally sags open during the active dying phase. Every clinical detail you learn makes you a better nurse! [learn more](GNS221_U4_T4#GNS221_U4_T4_h6)

question: Why is a pressure bandage placed on the arm right after an implant procedure?

options.A: To keep the arm completely paralyzed for two weeks
options.B: To prevent the hormone from leaking into the air
options.C: To push the implant deep down into the bone marrow
options.D: To minimize bruising and swelling at the site

explanation: The pressure bandage acts as a gentle hug for the insertion site during the first 24 hours, keeping swelling and bruising down to a minimum. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h8)

question: Why must blood pressure be lowered slowly during a hypertensive emergency?

options.A: Rapid drops can cause dangerous lack of blood flow to vital organs
options.B: Fast drops trigger permanent damage to peripheral nerve endings
options.C: Slow reductions prevent the kidneys from excreting excess potassium
options.D: Gradual changes allow oral medications time to absorb fully

explanation: Well done! Dropping pressure too fast when the body is used to high levels can starve the brain and heart of blood flow and cause a stroke or heart attack. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T2#GNS223_U1_T2_h7)

question: Which of the following best describes continuous quality improvement in a nursing unit?

options.A: Making small, ongoing changes to solve identified problems and better patient care
options.B: Waiting for a major hospital disaster before updating any clinical rules
options.C: Keeping all nursing routines exactly the same for ten years
options.D: Punishing nurses whenever a patient complains about the food

explanation: You nailed it! Quality improvement is all about making steady, daily adjustments to our workflows to give our patients the best care possible. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T4#GNS312_U5_T4_h7)

question: What simple comfort measure can a nurse suggest for a patient dealing with dry mouth from these drugs?

options.A: Take small sips of water often or suck on sugarless sweets
options.B: Stop drinking all fluids for the rest of the day
options.C: Take your medication right before doing heavy exercise
options.D: Rinse your mouth with strong salt water every single hour

explanation: Brilliant nursing care! Frequent sips of water or sugarless candy keep those mucous membranes nice and comfortable without messing with their blood sugar. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T7#GNS223_U6_T7_h7)

question: Which scenario is an example of natural passive immunity?

options.A: A patient recovering completely from a severe bout of malaria
options.B: A pregnant woman receiving a tetanus toxoid booster shot
options.C: An infant receiving protective antibodies through breast milk
options.D: A traveler receiving a shot of hepatitis B immunoglobulin

explanation: Passing antibodies from a mother to her baby via breast milk or the placenta is a natural way to provide temporary passive protection. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h4)

question: Which of these patients has the highest risk of developing an obstetric fistula?

options.A: A young rural mother who laboured at home for three days without skilled help
options.B: A middle-aged woman being treated for an uncomplicated bladder infection
options.C: A pregnant woman who attends all her routine antenatal care appointments
options.D: An older woman scheduled for an elective Caesarean section at a tertiary hospital

explanation: Spot on! Days of unmanaged labour without emergency care is the classic pathway to tissue damage and fistula formation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h2)

question: What action officially marks the start time of a 24-hour urine collection test?

options.A: Having the patient empty their bladder and discarding that urine
options.B: Drinking two large glasses of water right before the test starts
options.C: Saving the very first morning urine sample in the collection jug
options.D: Collecting all urine produced starting from midnight regardless of sleep

explanation: To get an accurate 24-hour count, we start with a totally empty bladder so we don't accidentally count old urine that sat in the body overnight! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T6#GNS123_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why might a surgeon sometimes create a temporary diverting colostomy during a fistula repair?

options.A: To make vaginal examinations easier for the nurse
options.B: To permanently replace the function of the rectum
options.C: To divert stool away from the healing surgical site
options.D: To allow the patient to eat solid food immediately after surgery

explanation: Diverting feces away from the repaired area protects the fresh sutures from contamination and promotes successful healing. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h7)

question: What is a common emotional response experienced by a person who has recently acquired a permanent physical disability?

options.A: Complete indifference toward their physical health status
options.B: Immediate and permanent acceptance of the new lifestyle
options.C: Euphoria over lifestyle changes and reduced responsibilities
options.D: Grief and a process similar to mourning a loss

explanation: Patients frequently experience a grief reaction as they process the loss of their previous physical abilities and independence. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h6)

question: Which of the following describes a standing plan in nursing?

options.A: A sudden emergency order that is never used again
options.B: A standardized guideline used repeatedly for recurring situations

question: What makes an IV fluid 'isotonic'?

options.A: It draws fluid out of the blood vessels and into the tissue cells
options.B: It contains large protein molecules that cannot cross membranes
options.C: It causes body cells to swell by forcing water inside them
options.D: It has the same particle concentration as blood plasma

explanation: You've got this! Isotonic fluids match the natural concentration of our blood, meaning they safely boost fluid volume without causing water to rush into or out of our cells. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h1)

question: Which lab pattern is typical for untreated hypoparathyroidism?

options.A: Low serum calcium and low parathyroid hormone
options.B: Low serum calcium and high serum phosphate
options.C: High serum calcium and normal parathyroid hormone
options.D: High serum calcium and low serum phosphate

explanation: Without enough PTH to boost calcium, your blood calcium drops (hypocalcemia) and your PTH levels remain low. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T11#GNS222_U2_T11_h4)

question: Why is 'Risk for Infection' a top concern when a patient's white blood cell count is low?

options.A: The patient is forced to share a room with other sick individuals
options.B: The body lacks sufficient defense mechanisms to fight off invading pathogens
options.C: Intravenous lines always cause immediate blood infections
options.D: Hospital linens usually harbor resistant bacterial strains

explanation: White blood cells are our frontline soldiers against germs. When numbers are down, even friendly germs can become a big problem. Protection is key! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h3)

question: What does a U&E panel primarily assess in a patient?

options.A: Kidney function and electrolyte balance
options.B: Thyroid hormone production
options.C: Liver enzymes and clotting factors
options.D: Red and white blood cell counts

explanation: A U&E test specifically targets kidney health, hydration levels, and chemical minerals in the blood. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T9#GNS123_U2_T9_h1)

question: Why is the very first cell division in oogenesis uneven or asymmetric?

options.A: Only the smaller cell is capable of surviving outside the ovary
options.B: One daughter cell keeps almost all the cytoplasm while the other becomes a tiny polar body
options.C: The cell divides without copying its DNA properly
options.D: Both daughter cells end up with different numbers of chromosomes

explanation: Think of it as sharing resources wisely. The egg keeps almost all the cytoplasm and nutrients, while the waste genetic material goes into a tiny polar body. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T9#GNS121_U5_T9_h5)

question: What part of the body does an intravenous pyelography (IVP) mainly check?

options.A: The nervous system
options.B: The urinary system
options.C: The digestive system
options.D: The respiratory system

explanation: You got this! An IVP is a special X-ray test that uses contrast dye to look closely at your kidneys, ureters, and bladder. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T16#GNS221_U2_T16_h1)

question: What is the main difference between an intermittent fever and a remittent fever?

options.A: Remittent causes chills, while intermittent only causes sweating
options.B: Remittent only happens at night, while intermittent has no schedule
options.C: Intermittent drops back to normal daily, while remittent stays high even though it fluctuates
options.D: Intermittent lasts for weeks, while remittent goes away in hours

explanation: Well done! The big clue is whether the temperature touches the normal baseline at least once during the day. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T6#GNS123_U3_T6_h4)

question: Why must nurses handle EENT physical assessments with extra care?

options.A: Patients are usually asleep under general anesthesia
options.B: Infection control rules don't apply to the face
options.C: These body parts have no nerves and cannot feel pain
options.D: The body parts are delicate, tightly packed, and connected

explanation: EENT organs have fragile tissues and important sensory spots, so you always want to use gentle hands and proper tools during exams. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T2#GNS311_U3_T2_h1)

question: At what angle should your needle enter the skin to create a smooth, curved stitch?

options.A: A downward 45-degree angle
options.B: A flat 15-degree angle
options.C: A completely parallel angle
options.D: A perpendicular 90-degree angle

explanation: Entering at a 90-degree angle lets the curved needle follow its natural circular shape, making it glide right through the skin smoothly. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T2#GNS311_U4_T2_h5)

question: How do migrating cancer cells manage to break into nearby blood vessels?

options.A: They secrete enzymes that break down surrounding tissue barriers
options.B: They attract white blood cells to carry them into circulation
options.C: They wait for the blood vessel walls to rupture from high pressure
options.D: They shrink in size until they slip through normal cell walls

explanation: Spot on! Cancer cells release special chemical enzymes that chew through tissue barriers and blood vessel walls, letting them slip right into circulation. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T2#GNS321_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is the main problem in a person with osteomalacia?

options.A: Excessive breakdown of cartilage by osteoclasts
options.B: Inadequate mineralization of the bone matrix
options.C: Autoimmune destruction of the synovial lining
options.D: Overgrowth of bone spurs along joint margins

explanation: In osteomalacia, the bone framework is there, but it fails to harden properly because of a lack of calcium or vitamin D. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T20#GNS222_U1_T20_h4)

question: What do we call the process where the uterus shrinks back to its normal, non-pregnant size?

options.A: Involution
options.B: Diastasis
options.C: Atrophy
options.D: Lochia

explanation: Great job! Involution is just the medical term for the uterus quickly returning to its pre-pregnant state through steady contractions. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h2)
